page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by fourth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 6455B). The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores at a sustained all-core frequency of 3.9 GHz, supported by 60 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES-NI and VAES.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In synthetic throughput testing, this memory subsystem reaches 224.53 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 104.52 GB/sec in large-block write operations, placing memory throughput in the top 25 percent of tested systems. The platform does not bundle local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, and provides a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread and compute capabilities driven by the 3.9 GHz clock rate. The r7iz.8xlarge achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2232.0, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, alongside a multi-core score of 18076.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 49575.64. The integrated AMX instructions and high memory throughput enable solid performance in CPU-based machine learning inference, generating 381.58 tokens per second on small (135M) language models and 28.25 tokens per second on medium (7B) parameter models.

The r7iz.8xlarge is well structured for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational database management systems with per-core licensing constraints, and memory-bound analytics. Because local disk storage is absent, architectures requiring persistent low-latency scratch space must account for network storage constraints.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6455B processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, contributing to a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2232.0 and strong uncached memory read bandwidth of 224.53 GB/sec. The instance lacks local storage, depending entirely on network storage, and maintains a 12 Gbps network baseline. Without bundled GPUs, the r7iz.8xlarge is positioned for compute-heavy, memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, real-time analytics, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
